items.title: What the ticket says

props.text: #174: afkv2: living cards, a view for outsiders, and stakeholder questions in the grill

## Pain

- A page holds the current state only in maps. An info card folds into "settled" after its round, so the design state cannot stay in view and evolve round after round.
- The human often cannot answer a grill point: the answer sits with a product owner, a tester, a director or another team. Nothing tracks those questions, and the page shows internal ids, rounds and decisions that an outsider cannot read.

## Idea (to be grilled)

- Page format v2: standing cards (living, updated in place, annotatable) and a brief view for outsiders.
- Grill: track the questions for other stakeholders, each with its context, why we need the answer, and simple examples; a stakeholder page to show on a shared screen; answers captured as notes on that page; the exit gate blocks on an open question unless the human accepts an assumption.

items.title: The 5 pains this ticket removes

props.text: The page becomes a document of the whole topic, from the overview down to the detail, one section per part, each kept current. The open question is where the round's questions go. I recommend A: your scope page did this (one card held the open questions, the other cards explained), and it keeps the questions first.

columns: A: questions on top, sections below
B: each question inside its section

props.text: One block of this round's questions right after your notes and my answers. Each question names its section and links to it; each section shows a chip such as '2 open questions'. Cost: the context is one click away.
Each question sits in the section it belongs to; the top lists links to them. Cost: the questions spread over a long page, and you scroll to find them.

items.title: Where this round's questions sit on a page that shows everything

props.text: From the first round, the page holds a section for every part of the topic I can see, even one the questions have not reached. A part not yet discussed says so and shows what I know so far. So a thought you have now has a place to land, and I read it when that part comes up. When you or I find a new part, it gets a section in the next round.

items.title: Every part of the topic has a section from round 1

settled.reading: Accepted, and sections are not fixed: they grow, shrink or change from any note or answer, also one on another section; a section that depends on others links to them.

props.text: Today a note with no element binds the rest of the session as a rule. Your notes will be ideas, corrections, feedback and rules, mixed and in any order. I recommend A.

columns: A: I read each note and say how I read it

props.text: I sort each note: an answer, a correction, a new idea, a rule for the rest of the session, or a question to me. My reply opens with that reading, such as 'Read as a new idea for the export section'. You correct me with a note when I am wrong. Cost: one wrong reading costs one round.
You start a note with a word such as 'rule:' or 'idea:'. No guessing on my side. Cost: you must remember the words, and a note without one still needs a reading.
A note on a section or with no element binds the session. Cost: a loose idea becomes a rule.

items.title: How I read a note that answers no question

settled.reading: Picks A, not rigid: one note can carry several readings at once, such as an answer, a new idea and a question; my reply states each one.

props.text: You want every change kept in view, growing round after round. The page rules today say: replace a stale fact, do not leave it struck beside the new one. I recommend A.

columns: A: one change list, never folded

props.text: One list 'What changed', newest round first, every round open: one line per change, each linking to its section. Each section heading carries the rounds it changed in. Sections show only the current text; a section's older text is in its own closed history. Cost: the list grows long.
The current and the previous round open, older rounds folded but counted. Cost: older changes take a click.
Old text struck beside the new text, with a round badge, as on your scope page. Cost: sections get harder to read, and it breaks a page rule we chose.

props.text: Either way, the outsider sees only the questions for others, in plain form: no rounds, ids, kinds or marks, and no notes of ours. I recommend A, but it rests on a fact I could not check: whether lavish takes notes from 2 browser tabs of one page into one send.

columns: A: a view of the grill page

props.text: A button or link opens the grill page in an outsider view, in its own browser tab, so the tab you share never shows the internal page. Your notes on a question land on the grill page, and one wait reads them. Cost: needs that lavish fact.
A separate page with its own link, which you can also send to someone. Cost: a second wait; on Codex the wait follows only the page shown last, so after a meeting you would type one chat line.

items.title: One page with an outsider view, or a separate page

settled.reading: Neither A nor B: the questions for others are one section of the grill page, written so an outsider can read it; no separate view or page.

props.text: The outsider view groups the questions by role, and you can show one group only, so the product owner does not see the questions for the director. A question for 2 roles shows in both groups.

items.title: Questions grouped by who to ask, one group at a time

settled.reading: One section for all questions, with a filter by who to ask; the order of the questions matters, since one answer can shape the next question.

props.text: Your call in chat: 'Block, allow assumption'. Written out:

- The grill's end check fails while any question for others is open.
- It counts as closed when it is answered, when you drop it with a reason, or when you accept an assumption I wrote for it on a card.
- An assumed answer goes into the requirements document as a risk, marked as assumed and naming who still has to confirm it.

items.title: The grill cannot end while a question for others is open

props.text:
- **In:** the page engine, use-lavish and visualize, so every skill's page can show the whole topic; the grill uses it, and gets questions for others.
- **Spinoff:** the solution-design skill adopting sections and questions for others in its own content; it gets the new page layout for free once use-lavish owns layout.
- **Out:** the plan approval page, which stays one sign-off card.

props.text: Your 2 notes, as I read them. The open part was the banner: I keep it, because it is where you start a round.

- A section or card always shows its current text.
- Under it, its own list of changes, one line per round it changed in, newest first, each with its cause: your note, an answer to a question, an answer from someone else, or something I found.
- The banner of the round lists what changed in this round only, each line linking to its section.
- No list of every change of every round.

items.title: Each section shows its own changes; the banner still lists this round's

props.text: The section sits on the grill page, as you said. On a shared screen the rest of the page is one scroll away, with its ids and our own decisions. So the section gets one button, 'Show only this section', that hides the rest of the page until you press it again, and the filter by who to ask works in that state too. Reject it if scrolling to the section is enough for you.

items.title: A button shows only the questions for others while you share your screen

settled.reading: No hide button. Each question for others links to the sections that help the discussion; what stays out is our internal shorthand, such as a decision number, which an outsider cannot read (and you need a tooltip for).

props.text:
- I order the questions so that an answer that shapes another question comes first.
- A question that depends on another says so and links to it, such as 'ask after: which roles may export'.
- You move a question with a note; I keep your order from then on.
- The filter by who to ask keeps the order.

items.title: I set the order of the questions; you change it with a note

props.text:
- In the meeting you write the answer as a note on the question, in your own words.
- **Who answered:** the role your note names; else the question's only role; else I ask you.
- **When:** the day you sent it.
- **A partial answer** keeps the question open, with what is now known in its context.
- **A follow-up** the answer raises joins the list, right after it.
- **Next round:** each point the answer touches comes back as a card for you to confirm, and each section it changes lists the cause, such as 'answer from the product owner'.
An answer from someone else is still your relay, so I never settle a point on it alone: you confirm the card.

items.title: How an answer you write down becomes part of the grill

props.text: When no page can show, or a skill runs without lavish, I print the same content as Markdown in chat: each section as a heading with its changes, this round's questions with their ids, and the questions for others in their order, each with all its parts. You answer in chat. Only the layout and the pictures are lost.

items.title: Without lavish, the same content comes in chat

settled.reading: Not a chat dump. Without lavish, the skill keeps the whole picture in its own context and asks round by round, each question with only the context it needs; with lavish, it lays the whole picture out. Same content, different presentation.
